brief.text:
TTP Market: Bullion · 2026-10-29

THE ASK (founder): a little stock-market-style experience, a simple order book where players buy, sell and trade items for tickles, hosted by a new character (a bull); simple, approachable, fun; players can see what their things are worth and what they made or lost; a playful way to learn how markets work while trading pig to pig.

ONE SENTENCE: Post the price you'll pay or take for a find, and Bullion matches you with a pig who agrees.

THE MONEY: tickles ready (the coin, N of 25). Pig to pig only: every tickle a buyer pays lands with a seller. The market mints nothing, burns nothing, and never touches the tickled count, snouts or the Board. On these boards the coin mark means tickles ready; the pink snout (row C only) means the tickled count.

CUT: Bullion's own shelf and moving quotes, news multipliers, a 'worth' on the whole bag, fees, quantity over 1, charts beyond the seven-day strip.

PICK: A as built / B / C · Bullion look A / B / C.

Boards link in Play: the fan's Market row, then the pinecone, then Buy now or Name your price. Art: Bullion's three looks plus cheer and shrug (Codex ImageGen), the real find glyphs, Rosie, Maya's Pepper, the Ghost Sheep.

s0.text:
Bullion · the host

WHAT: a loud, sunny bull who lives at the market all day. He hosts every deal and never buys, sells, holds or takes a cut. He reads yesterday's busiest find off real trades ('14 pinecones changed hooves yesterday, last at 5'), says one tip per visit, and cheers both sides of every deal, whoever did better.

PILLAR: Connect (he names the pig on the other side of your deal) · Collect (the finds he talks about are the twelve you dig).

CHARTER CHECK: a character, never a currency · painted sticker in the Ghost Sheep's hand, never emoji · the two NPCs never blur: one hosts and is always there, one collects and comes once a day. The Sheep's fancy is why two pigs value one pinecone differently, which is why they trade.

SERVER: nothing for him alone; his chatter is market_status().chatter (yesterday UTC, the busiest find, its last price).

CLIENT: BullionArt with three poses (idle, cheer on a fill, shrug on a quiet board or a moved price), g_bullion for the fan row, the rotating tips in constants/market.ts.

PICK: A (visor, waistcoat, chalk slate; the slate's line can follow the chatter) · B (boater, bow tie, bell) · C (apron, spectacles, scale). Recommended: A.

sA.text:
A · Bullion's Market (building this)

ONE SENTENCE: Post the price you'll pay or take for a find, and Bullion matches you with a pig who agrees.

WHAT: a pig-to-pig order book for the twelve finds, one per offer, priced in tickles ready (the coin). Per find: Pigs selling (cheapest first) and Pigs buying (highest first); ties go to the earliest; a friend is named, anyone else is 'a pig'. Last sold for (a real trade, never a quote), a seven-day strip, and the Ghost Sheep's price as the anchor. Buy now / Sell now take the best offer at 'at most' / 'at least' the price you saw (worse answers 'the price moved'). Name your price rests 24 h, cancel any time; an offer that meets the board fills at once at the price already waiting. Receipts: Paid 4 · sold for 6 · up 2, or Dug it up · sold for 6. Ledger: spent 23 · took in 31.

PILLAR: Collect first (buy the find you're missing, a third pinecone for a trade-up, a friend's wish) · Connect (every trade has a pig on the other side; 'Maya bought your pinecone for 5'). Contend untouched: no Board points move.

CHARTER CHECK: no new currency (the coin) · pig to pig only: every tickle a buyer pays lands with a seller, the market mints nothing and burns nothing · never the tickled count, snouts or the Board · finds only, never cosmetics or anything bought with money · no fee · no red losses, no shame states (a lapsed offer is a quiet line).

SERVER: 20261030120000_bullions_market.sql. market_offers / market_trades / market_receipts; satchel_items gains cost + source 'market'. market_status, market_book, market_place (nonce-idempotent, per-find advisory lock, price then time, never yourself, fills at the resting price, price_moved + best), market_cancel, dev_market_seed. app_settings.market_tuning: 4 open offers, 24 h, band 1 to 3x the Sheep's price (commons 1 to 9), 30 posts a day. Ships dark; turns on after The Feast's flip (2026-11-09).

CLIENT: constants/market.ts, utils/market.ts (fail-soft: an un-pushed server reads as closed), hooks/useMarket.ts, app/market.tsx + components/market/* (slate, find page, stepper, receipt, BullionArt), a Market row on the Barn fan while enabled.

FLOW IN PLAY: fan Market row > the market > pinecone > Buy now (receipt) or Name your price (sheet). Tin whistle row > quiet moments.

OPEN: which tickles (built: the coin) · Bullion's look · name strangers, or keep 'a pig' until a trade.

sB.text:
B · Market day (alternative)

ONE SENTENCE: Post what you'll pay or take before the evening bell; at six Bullion rings it and every find clears at one price.

WHAT: sealed offers all day (you see how many pigs are in, never a price); at 18:00 one clearing price per find; everyone who matched trades at it; unmatched offers come home.

WHY IT'S ATTRACTIVE: no sniping and no camping the board · every pig who traded a pinecone today got the same price, so nobody feels fleeced · a daily rendezvous: the bell is a reason for the herd to show up together, and it gives Bullion a big moment.

WHY NOT FIRST: you wait up to a day to trade (a friend's wish can't be bought now) · less of the stock-market feel the founder asked for: no live board, no Buy now · thinner learning of buying vs selling: one price hides the gap · a scheduled clear and a clearing algorithm to build and test.

PILLAR: Collect · Connect (the bell is a shared moment).

CHARTER CHECK: same money and limits as A; pig to pig, mints nothing.

SERVER: A's tables plus a pg_cron clear at 18:00 computing the uniform price per find (the price that matches the most finds).

CLIENT: sealed-offer page, the bell reveal, the results page. Could layer on A later as a weekly event.

sC.text:
C · Bullion makes the market (the first draft, cut)

WHAT: Bullion as an NPC market maker. A real shelf (he only resells what pigs sold him), his own 'I pay 2 · I ask 4' quotes moved by his stock and a daily news headline, pig offers inside his spread, money = the tickled count (the pink snout), and a 'worth' on your whole bag.

WHY CUT (Codex and ChatGPT, independently):
· Moving NPC prices mint tickles over time: buy from him at the bottom, sell back at the top, every cycle. His top bid even beat the Sheep's 20.
· A global shelf is easy to corner: seven units hit the stock clamp, so a few pigs can empty it or flood it.
· Scheduled news rewards camping the reset.
· 'Worth 12 now · up 2' promised liquidity nobody had: he might not buy all of it, or stop buying.
· Spending the tickled count spends the leaderboard, and friends could move Board points by overpaying.

KEPT FROM IT: Bullion himself, the Ghost Sheep's fancy as the reason values differ, a cost on every find, friends named.

PILLAR it claimed: Collect, and Contend by accident (the Board). CHARTER: failed fairness by construction.
